mechanism_narrative: A persistent uptick in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next month will raise weekday footfall near commercial districts and lift RETAIL_REC above the last four weeks. The signal is a return of commuting intensity rather than leisure-only movement.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES turned positive in t-1w and t-0w while TRANSIT moved from -3.4 to -0.7
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 28-day mean after four weeks despite continued positive WORKPLACES and TRANSIT readings.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains near zero or negative, residents substitute toward local errands and neighborhood shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks. This mechanism fails if higher home-staying does not translate into local retail visits.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 4 points while TRANSIT is at or below 0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 4.4 at t-0w and TRANSIT is -0.7
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays above 4 and TRANSIT stays nonpositive.

mechanism_narrative: A worsening PARKS indicator relative to its recent level signals weaker outdoor leisure demand, which diverts less spillover spending into malls and entertainment venues and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The claim fails if park mobility stabilizes or recovers without a retail decline.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20 points week-on-week or stays below -18 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is -19.7 at t-0w after -21.1 at t-2w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks while PARKS remains near or below its current depressed range.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below baseline, the city is not seeing a full commuting rebound and retail demand should stay subdued or soften over the next month. The mechanism is a lagged mobility constraint on shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below 0 while WORKPLACES stays below 2
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -0.7 and WORKPLACES is 1.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC improves above the prior 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM paired with stable or improving WORKPLACES indicates routine trip chaining and practical errands, which should lift nearby retail-and-recreation visits within one week. This mechanism fails if shopping and commuting move together but retail stays weak.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 42 while WORKPLACES is positive
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is 42.0 and WORKPLACES is 1.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 42 and WORKPLACES remains positive.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to rise while RESIDENTIAL drifts lower, the balance of time shifts away from at-home activity toward out-of-home spending, which should push RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks. The hypothesis fails when commuting increases but residential time does not ease.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -2.0 at t-2w to 1.4 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL eased from 5.9 to 4.4
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its last-four-week average despite a further rise in WORKPLACES and a decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT breaks above its recent near-zero range, retail-and-recreation should improve with a short lag because higher station usage restores access to shopping districts. If transit remains muted, the effect on retail stays weak.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above 0 after being negative in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -3.4 at t-3w to -0.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above zero from a negative prior week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in PARKS and TRANSIT signals a broader leisure-and-access rebound that supports higher retail visitation over the next month. The claim is falsified if outdoor and transport mobility recover but retail does not follow.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 4 points and TRANSIT rises by at least 1 point from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -21.1 at t-2w to -19.7 at t-0w and TRANSIT moved from -3.4 to -0.7
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC stays below its prior 28-day mean after four weeks despite simultaneous improvement in PARKS and TRANSIT.
